# After a cherry-pick nothing has reconciled the worktree: the objects moved, the
# revealed files did not. Sealing then writes the pre-pick plaintext back over the
# picked objects. `sesam seal` cannot tell that apart from a hand-resolved merge,
# so it warns instead of refusing - and this is what the warning is protecting.

sesam-repo admin base.txt changed.txt

cp $TMPDIR/base.txt s
cp $TMPDIR/base.txt t
exec sesam add s --group admin
exec sesam add t --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add secrets'

exec git checkout -b topic
cp $TMPDIR/changed.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'topic: change s'

exec git checkout master
cp $TMPDIR/changed.txt t
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'master: change t'

exec git cherry-pick topic

# The picked object is CHANGED, our plaintext is still BASE.
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/s.sesam
stdout 'CHANGED'
exec cat s
stdout 'BASE'

exec sesam seal
stderr 'the last audit entry is a merge'
stderr 'run .sesam reveal. first'

# The warning is not idle: the picked content is gone from the object now.
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/s.sesam
stdout 'BASE'

# Sealing again is quiet - the log no longer ends on a merge, and there is
# nothing left out of sync either.
exec sesam seal
! stderr 'WARNING'

-- base.txt --
line one
BASE
line three
-- changed.txt --
line one
CHANGED
line three
